classification.difficultyReason: Establish two triangle congruences and use the opposite-sides test to prove that an internal quadrilateral is a parallelogram.

content.prompt: In the diagram to the right, $ABCD$ is a parallelogram. $AC$ is a diagonal and $P$ and $Q$ are points on $AC$ such that $AP=CQ$. Prove that $PBQD$ is a parallelogram.

spec.description: Outer parallelogram ABCD, with single parallel arrows on AB and DC and double arrows on AD and BC. Red dashed AC contains P and Q in the order A, P, Q, C. Red dashed PB, BQ, QD and DP form the internal quadrilateral. Ordinary source-blue marks become house black; red retains the internal-line distinction.
spec.mathematics: AB parallel DC; AD parallel BC; A, P, Q, C are collinear; AP=CQ is supplied in the prompt.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied geometry, point labels, parallel marks and internal dashed segments are visible. No derived equalities or proof are shown.

answer.short:
$\triangle PAB\equiv\triangle QCD$ and $\triangle PAD\equiv\triangle QCB$ by SAS, so $PB=QD$ and $PD=QB$.

Both pairs of opposite sides of $PBQD$ are equal, so $PBQD$ is a parallelogram.
answer.worked:
In $\triangle PAB$ and $\triangle QCD$:
$$AP=CQ\quad\text{(given)},$$
$$AB=CD\quad\text{(opposite sides of parallelogram }ABCD\text{)},$$
$$\angle PAB=\angle QCD\quad\text{(alternate angles, }AB\parallel DC\text{)}.$$
Hence $\triangle PAB\equiv\triangle QCD$ by SAS, so $PB=QD$ (matching sides).

In $\triangle PAD$ and $\triangle QCB$:
$$AP=CQ\quad\text{(given)},$$
$$AD=CB\quad\text{(opposite sides of parallelogram }ABCD\text{)},$$
$$\angle PAD=\angle QCB\quad\text{(alternate angles, }AD\parallel BC\text{)}.$$
Hence $\triangle PAD\equiv\triangle QCB$ by SAS, so $PD=QB$ (matching sides).

Both pairs of opposite sides of $PBQD$ are equal. Therefore $PBQD$ is a parallelogram.
